answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a verifiable, costly identity credential before it can transact, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive rather than free. Think of reputation like a lagoon: calm on the surface but deep and hard to fake, since every past action leaves a trace. When a newcomer suddenly claims zenith-level trust without history, peers treat it as a ripple with no source — suspicious, not authoritative — and demand proof of work before granting it real influence.
